entries.name: European feather grass
entries.voxel_shape: dense tussock of thin blades with 3-4 tall plumed seedheads
entries.notes: The signature plant of the Pontic-Kazakh steppe: whole hillsides ripple silver in July. Drill seed spreads as a game mechanic.

entries.name: Silky needlegrass
entries.fruit: caryopsis with long naked flexuous awn
entries.voxel_shape: loose tussock of very fine blades, thin wiry seedheads
entries.notes: The needlegrass of drier steppe; the stiff awns can work into livestock skin. Pairs naturally with co-occurring feather grass.

entries.name: Wallis fescue
entries.leaves: evergreen, very fine rolled blades, grey-green
entries.voxel_shape: tight grey-green tuft, low wiry foliage, sparse flowering stems
entries.notes: One of the commonest tussock grasses of loess steppe; good early spring grazing before the feather grasses mature.

entries.name: Bulbous bluegrass
entries.leaves: deciduous, folded blades with bulbous base
entries.voxel_shape: low bright-green tuft with bulb-thickened stem bases
entries.notes: Often viviparous: bulbils replace seeds, so it spreads by breaking off and rolling. A weedy green flash after rain.

entries.name: Junegrass
entries.flowers: dense silvery spike-like panicle, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: fine tussock with one neat compact silver seed-spike each
entries.notes: Flowers early (hence 'June'), drought-tolerant and a favourite native restoration grass for degraded plains.

entries.name: Crested wheatgrass
entries.voxel_shape: erect tuft of flat blue-green blades with a stiff comb seed-spike
entries.notes: Workhorse of steppe reseeding and dryland pasture; spreads by rhizome and outcompetes weeds on disturbed ground.

entries.name: Smooth brome
entries.voxel_shape: loose upright clump of broad flat blades, tall soft panicle tops
entries.notes: Aggressive rhizomatous sod-former, planted for hay and roadside stabilization; escapes into native steppe.

entries.name: Chinese wildrye
entries.voxel_shape: coarse rhizomatous bunch of stiff blue-green blades and tall spikes
entries.notes: Backbone grass of Inner Mongolian typical steppe; handles grazing and saline soils better than most natives.

entries.name: Scaly needlegrass
entries.voxel_shape: very low dense tuft pressed to the ground, short spiky seedheads
entries.notes: C4 grass that thrives under heavy grazing; the dominant understorey of degraded Mongolian steppe. Nearly invisible until you step on it.

entries.name: Western wheatgrass
entries.voxel_shape: rhizomatous blue-green sod with stiff upright spike stems
uses: state grass of the Great Plains
entries.notes: The state grass of North Dakota; cool-season rhizomatous wheatgrass binding mixed-grass prairie soils.

entries.name: Blue grama
entries.voxel_shape: low tussock whose flattened seedheads curl sideways like eyebrows
entries.notes: Warm-season grama of the shortgrass steppe; curling seed-spikes are an easy silhouette to model.

entries.name: Buffalograss
entries.leaves: deciduous, fine short blades forming sod
entries.voxel_shape: short dense stoloniferous sod, only a few cm tall
entries.notes: The shortgrass champion of the High Plains; forms a tight mat under hooves where nothing else thrives.

entries.name: Needle-and-thread
entries.leaves: deciduous, inrolled wires with long thread-awns
entries.flowers: open panicle with twisted awns, midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: tussock bristling with very long thread-like awns that coil and uncoil
entries.notes: Famous for seeds that drill themselves into soil and livestock fur; awns keep twisting as humidity cycles.

entries.name: Little bluestem
entries.leaves: deciduous, flat blades and bronze flowering stems
entries.voxel_shape: upright bluish summer tuft turning copper-red in autumn
entries.notes: Premium autumn colour of the North American steppe-prairie edge; changes two colours across the season.

entries.name: Coirón blanco
entries.leaves: evergreen, hard grey wires forming large tussocks
entries.voxel_shape: big pale-grey hemispherical tussocks scattered across bare ground
entries.notes: Iconic tussock of Patagonian steppe; tough fibre protects it from grazing, so palatability swings the steppe's grazing value.

entries.name: Red oat grass
entries.voxel_shape: tufted grass that blushes red-bronze when in seed
entries.notes: The heart of southern African highveld veld; overgrazing replaces it with increaser grasses and bare crust.

entries.name: Fringed sagebrush
entries.voxel_shape: low silvery aromatic cushions dotted over grassland
entries.notes: Overgrazing indicator: when fringed sagebrush spreads, the steppe is being eaten down. Aromatic when brushed.

entries.name: Big sagebrush
entries.voxel_shape: knee-to-chest-high woody domes with silvery three-lobed leaves
entries.notes: The sagebrush steppe of the western US is a biome of its own; deep taproot, centuries-old individuals, poor fire recovery.

entries.name: Dwarf Russian almond
entries.flowers: bright pink, before the leaves, early spring
entries.voxel_shape: waist-high dome bursting pink in early spring, then plain green
entries.notes: Formerly Amygdalus nana. One of the few shrubs that colours the bare steppe pink before the grass greens up.

entries.name: Pygmy peashrub
entries.leaves: deciduous, tiny paired leaflets, spine-tipped twigs
entries.voxel_shape: low dense spiny thorn-cushion, yellow-flowered in June
entries.notes: Leguminous dwarf shrub of desertified Mongolian steppe; fixes nitrogen where the grass is failing.

entries.name: Russian thistle
entries.voxel_shape: round spiny bush that snaps off and rolls with the wind
entries.notes: The original tumbleweed: a steppe halophyte that escaped to America and became the ranch-country icon. Model the roll, not the plant.

entries.name: Leadplant
entries.voxel_shape: low silver-leaved shrub with dense violet bottle-brush spikes
entries.notes: Named for lead-coloured foliage; a nitrogen-fixing half-shrub signalling healthy intact prairie-steppe.

entries.name: Russian olive
entries.voxel_shape: small wind-shaped tree with shimmering silver foliage
entries.notes: Silver glint from a distance. Planted as shelterbelts across the dry steppe; invasive far outside its range.

entries.name: Black poplar
entries.voxel_shape: tall broad columnar poplar lining steppe rivers and oxbow lakes
entries.notes: The only tall tree of the open steppe, marking every river and old floodplain from miles away.

entries.name: Siberian elm
entries.voxel_shape: medium round-crowned elm, often wind-pruned, dark trunk
entries.notes: Fast, hardy and drought-proof; the tree of the steppe shelterbelt programs, now naturalized worldwide.

entries.name: East European tulip
entries.flowers: large red goblets, often single, spring
entries.voxel_shape: low cupped red cups on short stems, best in drifts
entries.notes: Schrenck's tulip (T. schrenkii) is its look-alike. Wild steppe tulips are the ancestors of every garden tulip; picking them is banned in many regions.

entries.name: Fernleaf peony
entries.flowers: dark red bowl flowers, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: fern-like green dome topped by deep red bowls
entries.notes: The steppe's showiest forb, blooming for two weeks on untouched loess slopes; a flagship of steppe reserves.

entries.name: Volga adonis
entries.flowers: yellow cups with dark base, spring
entries.voxel_shape: tiny fern-leaved herb with a single waxy yellow cup
entries.notes: Contains cardiac glycosides like the whole genus; historically a heart medicine, deadly in meadow hay.

entries.name: Dwarf bearded iris
entries.voxel_shape: low fans of iris leaves with one purple bearded bloom each
entries.notes: Miniature iris in two colour forms (violet and yellow) on open loess and rocky steppe; survives drought underground.

entries.name: Narrow-leaf coneflower
entries.flowers: pink-purple daisy with spiky cone, summer
entries.voxel_shape: bristly stems with drooping lilac petals around an orange cone
entries.notes: Flagship medicinal plant of the mixed-grass steppe; the cone centre is a seed-buffet for goldfinches.

entries.name: Field eryngo
entries.voxel_shape: spiny silver-blue globe on a stiff branched skeleton; rolling tumbleweed when dead
entries.notes: The original European tumbleweed: snaps at the base at maturity and rolls, scattering seed across the steppe.

entries.name: Mongolian onion
entries.voxel_shape: tight tufts of dark hollow leaves, white-violet pompom tops
entries.notes: Heavily grazed by sheep and horses; its onion smell betrays overgrazed steppe to anyone walking through.

entries.name: Russian rubber dandelion
entries.leaves: deciduous, rosette of greyish-green jagged leaves
entries.voxel_shape: common-dandelion look-alike with slightly greyer, smaller leaves
uses: rubber latex (up to 14% of root dry weight)
entries.notes: The Soviet answer to rubber shortages: root latex nearly identical to rubber-tree latex. Revived for EU rubber projects.

entries.name: Narrow-leaved foxtail lily
entries.flowers: dense 1 m pale-yellow raceme, early summer
entries.voxel_shape: bare strap-leaved rosette then a single tall yellow candle spike
entries.notes: The steppe's rocket: a 1 m yellow spike erupts from bare rock for three weeks in June, then vanishes entirely.

entries.name: Pasqueflower
entries.leaves: deciduous, velvety divided leaves after bloom
entries.flowers: erect violet bell, hairy stems, spring
entries.voxel_shape: small furry violet bells on silver stems above dry grass
entries.notes: One of the first flowers of the steppe spring, opening in thawed snow patches; protected across much of Europe.

entries.name: Prairie prickly pear
entries.voxel_shape: flat low pads hugging the ground, scattered through grass
entries.notes: The hardiest cactus on the continent: rides out Dakota winters below the snow line. Watch players' ankles.

entries.name: Soapweed yucca
entries.leaves: evergreen, stiff blue-green blades with fibrous threads
entries.voxel_shape: starburst rosette of sharp recurved leaves, tall white candle when blooming
entries.notes: Yucca-moth pollinated; the razor leaves slice livestock. Digging the roots yields usable soap.

entries.name: King oyster mushroom
entries.voxel_shape: stubby thick-stemmed oyster mushroom on eryngium and ferula roots
entries.notes: Grows on the roots of steppe umbellifers (eryngo, ferula); the strongest-flavoured cultivated oyster and the steppe's edible prize.

entries.name: Bladder saltbush
entries.voxel_shape: low grey mound with papery bladder bracts
entries.notes: Marker of the chenopod steppe of southern Australia; indicates heavy salty clays where little else survives.

entries.name: Ferula (asafoetida)
entries.voxel_shape: stout carrot-like herb throwing a thick stalk with yellow umbrella top
entries.notes: The source of hing: tapping the taproot resin, the entire spice trade for Indian curries. Sulfuric smell, irreplaceable in the kitchen.
